title: Asia stocks fall despite Wall Street records as rising oil, yields weigh
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com-- Asian stock markets fell on Wednesday, failing to join an overnight rally on Wall Street that took the S&P 500 and Nasdaq to record highs, as elevated bond yields and renewed gains in oil prices kept investors cautious.
The subdued Asian performance came even as U.S. stocks climbed overnight, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq setting record closing highs. The rally was led by technology and artificial-intelligence stocks.
U.S. stock index futures traded largely unchanged as of 02:55 GMT.
Elevated yields, higher oil drag Asia stocks lower
Japan's Nikkei 225 fell nearly 1%, while the broader TOPIX index edged 0.5% lower.
South Korea's KOSPI declined 1.2%, with heavyweight chipmaker SK Hynix (KS:000660) falling more than 2%. Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) shares dipped 0.6%.
Investors are cautiously awaiting Samsung and SK Hynix's quarterly results later in October, against very high expectations.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng slipped 0.8%, with the Hang Seng TECH sub-index dropping 1.3%.
Mainland Chinese markets remained closed for the National Day holiday, with trading due to resume on Thursday.
Investors remained wary of the bond market. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield remained around 5.3% on Wednesday, while the 30-year yield was above 5.6%, keeping longer-term borrowing costs close to multiyear highs.
Higher yields can reduce the appeal of equities, particularly in emerging markets, while increasing the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings.
Oil prices added to the pressure. Brent crude rose above $101 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate approached $90 as attacks by Iran-backed Houthi forces in Saudi Arabia heightened concerns about Middle East supplies.
The rise in crude prices revived concerns that higher energy costs could prolong inflation and constrain central banks' ability to ease monetary policy.
RBI rate decision, Fed minutes awaited
Elsewhere, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 traded flat, while Singapore's Straits Times Index traded flat.
Futures tied to India's Nifty 50 fell 0.5%.
Investors awaited the Reserve Bank of India's policy decision later on Wednesday, with the central bank widely expected to raise its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%.
The RBI has kept the rate at 5.25% for four consecutive meetings after cutting it by 125 basis points in 2025. Rising oil prices, a weaker rupee and higher global bond yields have intensified inflation risks, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra's comments on the outlook and the policy stance likely to be closely watched.
Investors were also awaiting the minutes of the Federal Reserve's September meeting later on Wednesday, along with speeches from several policymakers.
Markets have sharply reduced expectations for an October rate hike, with the probability of a 25-basis-point increase now around 20%, although an increase in December remains heavily priced.
Investors' focus was increasingly shifting to whether strong corporate earnings can offset the drag from higher energy prices and elevated global borrowing costs.

title: Oil prices rise with M.East, U.S. supply disruptions in focus
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com-- Oil prices rose on Wednesday as markets fretted over war-related supply disruptions in the Middle East and U.S. production outages stemming from the Atlantic hurricane season.
Crude extended gains from Tuesday, where increased fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and the Saudi Arabia-backed government in Yemen also spurred fears of supply disruptions, especially after the Houthis claimed to have attacked a major Saudi refinery.
Brent oil futures rose 0.77% to $101.36 a barrel by 21:15 ET (01:15 GMT), while West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 0.89% to $90.25 a barrel.
Reports of improving oil supplies from the Middle East limited bigger gains in crude, as did planned emergency supply releases by the Group of Seven.
Get more insights on oil markets by subscribing to InvestingPro-- with up to 50% off
M.East, Gulf of Mexico disruptions in focus
Iran was seen ramping up its pace of attacks in the Strait of Hormuz over the past week– a trend that came just as Gulf producers brought shipments from the region back to prewar levels.
Flows through Hormuz and the Middle East had risen sharply over the past few weeks, coming back in sight of pre-war levels, according to shipping data cited by Reuters. This came as the U.S. continued to offer naval protection against Iran in the region.
But the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported seven strikes on vessels around the waterway since late-September, with one strike coming as recently as Sunday.
Elsewhere, the Saudi-backed Yemen government was seen retaking several key points along the Red Sea from the Iran-backed Houthis this week. The move could eventually help increase crude supplies through the Bab el-Mandeb strait.
But the Houthis retaliated by attacking key targets in Saudi Arabia, including an Aramco refinery in Riyadh. Oil extended gains on Wednesday following fresh Houthi aggression against Riyadh.
Oil markets were also bracing for disruptions in North American production as forecasters warned an ongoing tropical disturbance in the Gulf of Mexico could become a storm by Friday.
The storm is likely to hit offshore oil production in the Gulf, with both Chevron and Shell seen evacuating non-essential personnel from offshore facilities in the region.
U.S. oil inventories fall after three weeks of builds- API
U.S. oil inventories fell 2.09 million barrels in the week to October 2, data from the American Petroleum Institute showed late-Tuesday.
The draw comes after three straight weeks of outsized builds, and comes as American producers brace for weather-related disruptions in the Gulf of Mexico.
The API data usually heralds a similar trend from official U.S. inventory data, which is due later on Wednesday.

title: Vance says Iran must reduce nuclear enrichment capacity to end war - Reuters
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com-- U.S. Vice President JD Vance said Iran must make a meaningful reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to meet Washington’s demands and end the seven-month war, signaling that concrete nuclear concessions will be central to any diplomatic settlement.
In an exclusive interview with Reuters on Monday, Vance said the U.S. would not accept Iranian assurances about future reductions and instead wanted Tehran to take tangible steps to scale back its enrichment program.
“If you don’t want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel?” Vance said, arguing that Iran could demonstrate its commitment to not developing a nuclear weapon by reducing its enrichment capacity.
Iran and the U.S. have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial route for global energy shipments.
President Donald Trump has rejected Tehran’s latest offer and warned that military operations could intensify after the November midterm elections.
Vance said Washington remained open to an agreement but would require concrete action from Tehran.
He also said Washington remained uncertain about who ultimately makes decisions in Tehran, despite talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi.

title: Gold holds gains as oil flows recover, Treasury yields ease
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com -- Gold prices held near $4,160 on Wednesday after rising 0.6% in the previous session, as improving oil supplies from the Middle East and a pullback in bond yields reduced pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates this month.
At 20:46 ET (00:46 GMT), XAU/USD fell 0.1% to $4,160.49 an ounce, while Gold Futures rose 0.03% to $4,188.22. XAG/USD was little changed at $61.36, while XPT/USD fell 0.2% to $1,708.06. The U.S. Dollar Index rose 0.1% to 101.95.
Higher Middle East oil flows ease rate concerns
Oil supplies from the Middle East have recovered to roughly four-fifths of pre-conflict levels, according to analysts and research firms, helping ease some concerns over an extended disruption to regional energy flows.
The improvement has helped stabilize oil prices and reduced some pressure on inflation and the Fed's rate outlook.
Still, risks to energy supplies remain elevated.
Iran has increased attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, while major oil executives have warned that the industry is running out of temporary measures to manage the disruption as the U.S.-Iran war approaches its eighth month.
Treasury yields also retreated on Tuesday after longer-dated maturities surged to fresh multi-decade highs a day earlier.
The decline in yields has provided some support for gold by reducing the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding metal.
Fed hike bets fade as gold remains below key averages
Federal Reserve officials have continued to push back against the likelihood of an imminent rate increase.
Traders are now pricing in a less than 20% probability of an October hike, down from about 40% a week earlier.
Minutes from the Fed's September meeting are due later Wednesday.
Policymakers raised borrowing costs at that meeting for the first time in three years, and the minutes could offer fresh clues on the direction of policy.
Gold remains in a relatively tight range in October and is trading below several closely watched price averages.
The metal is also down more than 20% since the U.S.-Iran conflict began in late February, highlighting the sharp reversal from earlier gains.

title: LG Electronics shares drop as Q3 prelim earnings miss estimates
full_text:
Investing.com-- LG Electronics (KS:066570) shares fell sharply on Wednesday after the company reported preliminary third-quarter operating profit that missed market expectations, despite posting year-on-year growth.
The South Korean electronics maker estimated third-quarter operating profit at 781.8 billion won ($583.8 million), up 13.5% from a year earlier, while revenue rose 8.9% to 23.83 trillion won.
Operating profit was about 17% below the 941.7 billion won average forecast compiled by Yonhap Infomax.
Seoul-listed shares of the company fell 7.7% to 214,500 yen by 03:21 GMT, reversing a strong gain in the previous session.
For the first nine months, revenue rose 9.2% to 71.38 trillion won and operating profit jumped 55.9% to 4.03 trillion won.
The preliminary figures exclude net income and remain subject to an external audit. LG is expected to provide further details when it releases its full third-quarter results later this month.

title: OCBC partners with Ant International on tokenised deposits
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com -- OCBC said on Wednesday it was partnering with Alibaba-backed Ant International on a tokenised deposit solution that allows continuous treasury management and liquidity movement between Singapore and Malaysia.
The solution enables Ant and its businesses to manage intra-group liquidity across borders, OCBC said in a press release.
Tokenised deposits are digital representations of commercial bank deposits on a distributed ledger. The technology uses blockchain to create a transparent and immutable audit trail, reducing manual reconciliation and improving operational efficiency.
Ant International will be able to move SGD- and USD-denominated tokenised deposits on a 24/7 basis, enabling near real-time settlements of treasury transactions between its entities. The solution uses OCBC’s blockchain capabilities and is delivered through Ant International’s WhaleRTP platform, a treasury management solution that optimises liquidity management while enabling interoperability across blockchain assets from financial institutions.
Traditional cross-border liquidity movements are often limited by batch processing cycles, operating-hour restrictions and currency and settlement cut-off times. The tokenised deposits allow companies to move and deploy liquidity beyond traditional banking windows.

title: U.S. stock futures steady after tech rally lifts S&P 500, Nasdaq to records
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures were little changed on Tuesday evening after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record closing highs, as investors turned their attention to Federal Reserve meeting minutes and the start of the third-quarter earnings season.
S&P 500 Futures inched 0.1% higher to 7,880.75 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures traded flat at 31,493.25 points by 20:03 ET (00:03 GMT). Dow Jones Futures were muted at 51,827.0 points.
In the regular session, the S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7,818.93, its first close above 7,800, while the NASDAQ Composite gained 0.5% to 27,599.79, extending its record run for a second session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.5% to 51,521.28.
AI-related technology stocks remained a key driver of the rally. Semiconductor shares, including Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), gained on optimism over demand for chips used in artificial intelligence infrastructure, while Nvidia remained close to a $6 trillion market valuation.
Constellation Energy (NASDAQ:CEG) also jumped after announcing a long-term electricity deal with Alphabet’s Google, underscoring investor enthusiasm for the power infrastructure needed to support data centres.
The gains came as Treasury yields pulled back from their recent highs. The 10-year Treasury yield ended Tuesday around 5.28%, down about 3 basis points, while the two-year yield fell to about 4.80%. The 10-year yield had climbed above 5.35% on Monday, its highest level since April 2002.
Investors are now awaiting the minutes of the Federal Reserve’s September meeting on Wednesday for clues on the debate over further interest-rate increases.
Expectations for another rate hike this month have fallen sharply following softer employment and inflation data. Interest-rate futures were pricing roughly an 80% probability of no change at the Fed’s October meeting, compared with expectations for a hike just a week earlier.
Oil prices also eased from recent highs, providing some relief to inflation-sensitive assets. Brent crude remained around $100 a barrel, while continued Middle Eastern oil shipments have helped prevent a sharper supply shock despite the prolonged conflict and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.
Investors are also preparing for the third-quarter earnings season, which begins in earnest next week.

title: Asian currencies mixed as dollar holds gains, yen weakens near 158
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com -- Asian currencies were mixed on Wednesday as the U.S. dollar held near recent highs, while the Japanese yen weakened toward 158 per dollar as markets weighed the Bank of Japan's policy outlook and renewed fiscal concerns.
Higher oil prices and rising Treasury yields kept pressure on the currency complex, while investors awaited the Federal Reserve's September meeting minutes and several Fed speakers for clues on the next rate move.
The U.S. dollar index was around 102.03, up 0.2%, while the USD/JPY pair rose 0.2% to 158.38. The EUR/USD pair fell 0.2% to 1.124, while the GBP/USD pair slipped 0.2% to 1.325. The Australian dollar was around $0.6973 and the New Zealand dollar at $0.5610.
Oil rose as much as 1% to around $101.50 a barrel after Iran increased attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, pushing Treasury yields higher. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose three basis points to around 5.31%.
Dollar awaits Fed minutes as hike bets retreat
The dollar has come under some pressure recently after softer U.S. PCE inflation and jobs data reduced expectations for an October rate increase, but markets continue to price further tightening later this year and in 2027.
The chance of a Fed hike of at least 25 basis points in October has fallen to 20.5% from about 51% a week ago, according to CME FedWatch, while markets still price an 84.5% probability of a December increase.
The Fed will release minutes from its September 15-16 meeting later Wednesday, when it raised rates to combat inflation.
Fed officials Christopher Waller, Neel Kashkari and Alberto Musalem are also due to speak. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said Tuesday that the central bank still needs to raise rates further to lower inflation.
Yen weakens as BOJ weighs fiscal risks
The USD/JPY pair remained around the mid-158s after a new BOJ board member, Ayano Sato, said she supports raising interest rates in several stages.
The BOJ could signal this month that underlying inflation has broadly reached its 2% target, according to reports citing people familiar with its thinking, highlighting its readiness to raise rates again.
DBS FX & Credit Strategist Chang Wei Liang said the yen could remain slightly weaker as the Japanese government considers a second supplementary budget.
Markets could react negatively because authorities had previously indicated another package was no longer planned and that reserve funds would instead be used for disasters and other emergencies, Chang said.
Rupee in focus ahead of RBI decision
The USD/INR pair rose 0.2% to 96.61, with the rupee under pressure from oil above $100 and higher U.S. yields.
The Reserve Bank of India is widely expected to raise rates by 25 basis points to 5.50%, its first increase since February 2023. Governor Sanjay Malhotra's comments will be closely watched for signals on the subsequent policy path.
DBS Senior Economist Radhika Rao said the macro backdrop has changed materially since the August meeting, with oil prices above $100 and the Fed already restarting its tightening cycle.
Rao said the key question is whether the move is simply a recalibration after last year's rate cuts or the beginning of a longer tightening cycle. DBS expects another hike in the fourth quarter, with the risk of additional increases rising as oil prices remain elevated and weather conditions stay unfavorable.
Across the region, the USD/CNH pair rose 0.05% to 6.7043, while USD/CNY was unchanged at 6.7046. The USD/KRW pair slipped 0.01% to 1,337.85 and the USD/SGD rose 0.12% to 1.2788.
Elsewhere, the euro was pressured by fresh concerns over European fiscal positions. French bond futures underperformed German equivalents as investors assessed the outlook for France's deficit, while Spain's snap-election concerns have added to broader pressure on the euro area.

title: Zscaler: Stifel hikes target on AI cybersecurity prospects
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com-- Stifel raised its price target on Zscaler Inc (NASDAQ:ZS) on Tuesday, saying the cybersecurity firm’s first analyst day since 2021 strengthened the case for its artificial intelligence prospects.
Stifel hiked Zscaler’s target to $235 from $200 and maintained its Buy rating on the stock.
Get top AI stock picks and insights by subscribing to InvestingPro
Zscaler hosted the event on Tuesday, where management outlined its strategy, broader product lineup, go-to-market priorities and mid-term financial model, Stifel analysts said in a note.
The analysts said management made a strong case for the growing importance of both securing AI and using AI to improve security. They said Zscaler’s zero-trust architecture was the right approach, given rising adoption of AI agents and agentic threats.
The biggest surprise was a fiscal 2031 annual recurring revenue target, Stifel said. They had expected management to focus only on mid-term profitability.
Zscaler gave a base case of more than $8 billion in ARR, a 17% compound annual growth rate, and an upside case of $10 billion, or 22% growth, on AI tailwinds.
Stifel said the base case looked achievable and was in line with fiscal 2027 guidance. The upside case would require a reacceleration in growth, which the brokerage said was possible but not something it was underwriting yet.
Profitability targets were largely in line with expectations. Zscaler guided to a fiscal 2031 operating margin of 27% to 30% and a free cash flow margin of 29% to 32%.
Management also reaffirmed its first-quarter and full-year fiscal 2027 targets, which the analysts called a positive after the recent change in chief revenue officer.
Stifel said Zscaler may have set a higher bar with the $10 billion target, but it left the event more positive on the company’s market opportunity, which management pegged at $220 billion.
The analysts said AI agents needed to be secured in a zero-trust manner to prevent lateral movement and agent misbehavior. They said that represented an emerging opportunity, given the unique data Zscaler sees and generates.
They added that Zscaler had several drivers to sustain at least mid-to-high-teens revenue growth and margin expansion in the coming years.

title: FOMC minutes ahead; Constellation Brands reports - what’s moving markets
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com - Futures linked to the main U.S. stock indices inch down, before the release of key minutes from the Federal Reserve’s latest policy gathering. Investors will be hunting for any insight into the Federal Open Market Committee’s policy trajectory, after rate-setters lifted borrowing costs at their September meeting. Elon Musk’s SpaceX reportedly looks to raise $40 billion to purchase more Nvidia chips. Shares of beer producer and marketer Constellation Brands retreat following quarterly earnings, while jeans manufacturer Levi Strauss is due to report.
1. Futures drop
U.S. stock futures pointed lower on Wednesday. By 02:56 ET (06:56 GMT), the Dow futures contract had dropped by 108 points, or 0.2%, S&P 500 futures were mostly unchanged, and Nasdaq 100 futures had dipped by 28 points, or 0.1%.
The main averages on Wall Street crept higher in the prior session, although the indices ended off their earlier highs.
A selloff in U.S. bonds took a breather, while a similar rout in France eased, soothing worries of contagion spreading in global debt markets. But analysts at Vital Knowledge suggested that investors remain skeptical that "this asset class can sustain a material rally," highlighting that a surge in artificial intelligence spending will likely coincide with a "tidal wave" of debt issuance. Benchmark 10-year U.S. and French bond yields moved higher.
Meanwhile, oil prices initially fell, fueling hopes that improving crude shipments out of the Middle East will ease energy-induced inflationary pressures. Yet crude prices eventually rebounded, with reports underlining the massive cost of ferrying oil through the Gulf and an ongoing global shortage of refined products.
2. FOMC minutes ahead
Traders are now looking ahead to the unveiling of minutes from the Fed’s meeting in September, when the central bank raised interest rates for the first time since 2023.
Official projections also hinted at more rate rises to come before the end of the year. Policymakers are keen to corral inflation, which has been hovering well above the Fed’s 2% target for months, due largely to the energy price jump caused by the Iran war.
Still, expectations have faded that the Fed will roll out another rate increase at its next gathering this month. Along with a selection of statements from Fed officials downplaying the urgency of an October hike, recent employment data came in softer than anticipated, likely keeping rate-setters wary of tightening policy so fast that it dents the wider economy.
In theory, raising borrowing costs can put a lid on price gains, albeit at the risk of weighing on the labor market and economic growth.
3. SpaceX to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips - FT
SpaceX is seeking to raise $40 billion in an endeavor led by Apollo Global to buy Nvidia chips, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Elon Musk’s rocket and artificial intelligence firm is seeking to raise about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt for the order, with Apollo expected to lead the deal and help market the debt, the FT report said.
Pimco was among a small group of lenders in talks to fund the deal, the FT reported.
The planned fundraise highlights the large sums that are being poured into data centers, chips, and other infrastructure needed to run AI.
SpaceX is closely tied to Nvidia, with Musk having earlier stated that it would exclusively use Nvidia chips in its Colossus data centers.
4. Constellation Brands slips after earnings
Shares of Constellation Brands fell in after-hours trading, despite the company, whose brands include beers like Corona and Modelo Especial, posting better-than-expected second-quarter profit and sales.
Net sales for the quarter ended on August 31 climbed 6% to $2.63 billion, while earnings per share on an adjusted basis stood at $3.74. Both outpaced Wall Street expectations, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters.
But beer depletions, a critical metric tracking when distributors sell brews to retail accounts, edged down by 0.6%, missing estimates by 70 basis points, analysts at TD Cowen flagged.
They added that management’s decision to reiterate its full-year financial guidance implies that second-half sales "will be down [roughly] 2% at the midpoint." August trends also slowed against a weaker consumer backdrop, likely leading to increased marketing investment in the final six months of the fiscal year, the analysts noted.
Constellation also said it will pay $75 million -- and potentially an additional $278 million over five years -- following the closure of a deal to acquire SpikedAde, a vodka-based ready-to-drink beverage firm.
5. Levi Strauss to report
On the earnings calendar, Levi Strauss is due to report after the closing bell, with the jeans maker banking on the appeal of its premium denim products among wealthier customers despite wider economic uncertainty.
Shares of Levi’s have edged down by more than 1% so far this year, even after the company lifted its full-year profit outlook in July.
Speaking to investors at the time, CEO Michelle Gass said that Levi’s, which has rolled out baggier styles to entice Gen Z shoppers and has focused on building its higher-margin direct-to-consumer business, was attempting to capture a "sizable premium segment" it has not already accessed.

title: Intel to continue working on Musk’s Terafab despite TSMC talks - Bloomberg
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com-- Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) will continue working with Elon Musk on Terafab, a project aimed at producing advanced semiconductors, Chief Executive Lip-Bu Tan told Bloomberg.
The report comes as speculation about a potential partnership with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) (TW:2330) raised concerns among investors.
Musk said earlier this week that he was in discussions with TSMC about collaborating on Terafab. Intel signed on as the project’s development partner in April.
Tan said Intel would remain involved in the project ahead of an event in Tokyo marking the U.S. chipmaker’s 50th year of operations in Japan, Bloomberg reported.
Terafab, a collaboration involving Tesla, SpaceX and xAI, is planned to include two factories, with one focused on chips for Tesla vehicles and humanoid robots and another intended to support AI data centres in space. The project ultimately targets one terawatt of computing capacity a year.
Terafab is part of a broader global push by governments and companies to expand semiconductor manufacturing capacity to meet surging demand driven by artificial intelligence.

title: RBI hikes rates for first time in nearly 4 years, opens door to more hikes
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
Investing.com -- The Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on Wednesday, its first rate hike since February 2023, as the central bank responded to a less favorable inflation outlook and heightened geopolitical risks.
The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) increased the policy rate from 5.25%, with the move broadly in line with economists’ expectations. The decision comes as global conditions remain challenging amid geopolitical events, while higher energy prices and other external pressures have complicated the inflation outlook.
InvestingPro: Get market insights and AI tools at 50% off this October
RBI turns hawkish, signals scope for further hikes
The rate hike was unanimous, while the MPC voted 4-2 to shift its policy stance from “neutral” to “calibrated tightening,” indicating that most members see room for further increases in borrowing costs.
Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the timing and extent of any additional increases would depend on how inflation and economic growth evolve.
The MPC said the Indian economy is expected to remain resilient, but noted that the inflation environment and its outlook are different from those seen last year.
Abhijit Surya, Senior APAC Economist at Capital Economics, said the hawkish tone of the decision supported the firm’s view that further tightening was likely.
Capital Economics expects 25-basis-point hikes in both December and February, which would take the repo rate to a peak of 6%, above the 5.75% terminal rate expected by consensus.
The RBI is also navigating a more difficult external backdrop, with geopolitical developments keeping global economic conditions uncertain and energy prices remaining a key risk for import-dependent India.
Inflation outlook worsens as growth remains resilient
The central bank expects headline consumer price inflation to average 5.8% over the next three quarters, including the current quarter. Core inflation, which excludes food and fuel, is projected at 4.4% for the current financial year.
The revised inflation outlook comes as price pressures have picked up. India’s consumer price inflation rose to 4.82% in August from 4.45% in July, while food inflation increased to 5.95% from 5.52%.
At the same time, the resilient domestic economy gives the central bank greater scope to prioritize inflation without responding to an immediate growth slowdown.
The central bank raised its growth forecast for the current financial year to 7.1%, up 40 basis points from its previous estimate. GDP expanded 7.8% in the April-June quarter, beating the RBI’s 7% forecast.
The Indian rupee strengthened slightly with the USD/INR pair falling by 0.2% to 96.59 rupee. India’s benchmark Nifty 50 index was last down 0.4% after the decision.
The rate increase marks a shift after a 125-basis-point easing cycle that began in February 2025. The RBI had kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% at its August meeting, after holding it at that level at its previous reviews.

title: IMF chief warns energy shock, growing debt and AI risks threaten global growth
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
By Rae Wee
SINGAPORE, Oct 7 (Reuters) - The global economy is under threat from persistently high energy prices, record public debt and risks from the AI investment boom, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned on Wednesday, urging governments to implement protective fiscal and monetary policy measures.
In a speech previewing IMF and World Bank Annual Meetings next week in Bangkok, Georgieva said the world was being pulled in two directions — a negative energy supply shock from the Middle East conflicts and a positive demand shock from artificial intelligence that is also fuelling inflation.
"The combined impact of these two forces is highly uneven across the world," Georgieva said, adding that the AI boom was bypassing many countries.
New IMF growth forecasts to be released during the Bangkok meetings will show the biggest growth downgrades will come in economies ravaged by war, Georgieva said. These include Ukraine, suffering significant damage to civilian and economic infrastructure, and Gulf countries hit by Iranian strikes and sharply reduced energy exports.
Georgieva did not indicate in her prepared remarks whether the IMF’s latest World Economic Outlook would change the overall 2026 global growth forecast from the sluggish 3.0% rate forecast in July.
That forecast, which predicted a rebound to 3.4% growth in 2027, assumed the Strait of Hormuz would start to reopen in mid-July and return to pre-war conditions by March 2027. It assumed oil prices would average $89 a barrel in 2026 and $78 a barrel in 2027.
Georgieva said oil prices remain at $100 a barrel, with impaired refining capacity adding another $100 in "crack-spread" margins per barrel for key products including diesel. The winter heating season will boost demand even as natural gas supplies remain restricted by threats to LNG shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, she added.
"Even if the war in the Gulf were to end soon, the problem of high energy prices will likely persist for some time," Georgieva said, adding that Brent crude oil futures predict high oil prices through 2027.
Higher energy prices are pushing up inflation, policy rates and benchmark bond yields, she said, noting that US, German and Japanese 10-year sovereign yields are now at their highest levels since 2007, 2009 and 1996, respectively, and still climbing.
GROWING DEBT LOAD
Adding to the worries to be discussed by the IMF’s 191 member countries next week is a growing public debt burden that is sapping growth and adding inflationary pressures, Georgieva said. The IMF says public debt is at the highest level since World War Two and is projected to exceed 100% of GDP before 2030.
Georgieva singled out advanced economies, led by the United States, as the "worst offenders" on debt loads, with debt-to-GDP ratios higher than emerging markets and low income countries.
Policymakers can no longer rely on higher growth rates alone to solve fiscal problems, she said.
"And yet we don’t see decisive action in the high-debt advanced economies where the need of the hour is for credible medium-term fiscal consolidation plans, supported in some cases by upfront fiscal measures, including to take some pressure off monetary policy," she said.
After five-and-a-half years of above-target inflation, Georgieva said inflationary pressures were persisting, from the AI build-out, energy and food price shocks, tariffs, higher defense spending and higher debt service costs.
"Now may be a good time for a prudently hawkish bias in many countries’ monetary policy," Georgieva said, adding that rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve, the ECB and the Bank of Japan were "highly appropriate."
In a fireside chat following her speech, Georgieva added that the "most important task" for monetary policy in the current environment is to focus on price stability and for central banks to communicate their resolve in maintaining it.
"They can only do it when central banks are independent, and when central banks resist pressure that may come from the fiscal side to ease the burden by basically stepping up, buying debt, making it so that the situation from the fiscal side eases," she said.
"I would call this monetary cowboys, running to the rescue of the fiscal agents, and my message is: please don’t."
AI RISKS ABOUND
Georgieva highlighted other risks from AI, where investment as a share of GDP is likely to exceed that of railroads, the electricity grids or telecommunications infrastructure.
The rising economic and financial concentration puts pressure on AI companies to deliver productivity and earnings gains to justify lofty valuations, she said, warning that market disappointment could turn into "a far-reaching shock."
But she said IMF research suggests that AI, done right, could add a half percentage point of extra world growth annually.
AI preparedness is key, she said, including regulatory guardrails that "help manage AI’s substantial perils, which include large-scale labor market fallout, serious cyber and stability risks and frontier models threatening to escape human control and run amok."
In addition to building fiscal strength, even at difficult political costs, Georgieva said governments should take other steps to boost growth, including reforms that would develop improved workforce skills, make corporate startups and wind-downs easier, boost energy security and streamline regulations.

full_text:
BRUSSELS, Oct 7 (Reuters) - The governing board of the International Energy Agency will hold an informal meeting at 1300 local time on Wednesday to discuss the proposed release of oil and diesel stocks, said two European Union diplomats.
The representatives of EU nations had already discussed this proposed release at a meeting on Wednesday morning, added the diplomats.
Under pressure from US President Donald Trump, the Group of Seven major economies agreed last week to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves and pledged to refrain from energy export restrictions.

Indian consumer price index inflation has consistently run above the RBI’s 2% to 4% medium-term target since June, with soaring oil prices– due to the Middle East war– being a main source of upside pressure.
A disrupted monsoon, due to the Super El Nino effect, also drove up Indian food prices, while local consumer demand– also a major inflationary driver– continued to push higher.

Capital Economics analysts said the decision supported their view that more interest rate hikes by the RBI were likely, with 25 bps hikes expected in both December and February.
Higher rates tend to weigh on equity markets, especially as local monetary conditions tighten. But they also tend to draw in more foreign capital.
Sectors like large banks and insurers stand to benefit from higher rates, while others such as utilities and autos face a negative outlook.
Tighter monetary conditions herald more headwinds for India’s already struggling stock markets, which are among the worst performers in the world so far in 2026. The Nifty is trading down more than 13% year-to-date.

title: Micron’s Taoyuan union in Taiwan secures authorisation to strike
full_text:
Wall Street ends at a record high for the first time since mid-August
By Wen-Yee Lee
TAIPEI, Oct 7 (Reuters) - A Taiwanese union representing workers at Micron Technology said on Wednesday it had secured authorisation from its members to strike work over a dispute concerning the company’s bonus scheme, escalating a labour conflict at the chipmaker’s largest manufacturing hub.
The union, which represents workers at Micron’s operations in the northern city of Taoyuan, said 1,994 members, or 99% of those casting ballots, voted in favour of a strike. It said details of any strike, including its timing, were still under discussion.
Taiwan is a crucial production centre for Micron’s DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, key components in AI servers. A labour action could amplify supply concerns in an already tight memory-chip market.
Micron employs about 15,000 people in Taiwan, with separate unions representing workers at its Taoyuan and Taichung operations.
Mediation with the Taoyuan union ended without agreement in September, while the Taichung union remains in negotiations.
Together, the two unions represent more than 80% of Micron’s Taiwan workforce.
Micron in September announced fiscal 2026 rewards for more than 60,000 employees globally following what it described as an "extraordinary year" for the company. That included employees in Taiwan receiving a T$1 million ($31,386.33) cash bonus.
However, the Taoyuan union said the package failed to address its demand for a permanent profit-sharing mechanism and criticised Micron for announcing them while labour mediation was underway without first reaching an agreement with the union.
($1 = 31.8610 Taiwan dollars)
